title: Iran's Supreme Leader Gets a Huge Funeral — What Does It All Mean?
summary: Have you ever seen a funeral that's also a political rally? That's what's happening in Iran right now. The country's former Supreme Leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, died in a US-Israeli airstrike back in February. Now, a week of ceremonies is using symbols to send messages. The official slogan is "We must rise," which comes from a verse in the Quran (the Muslim holy book). There's also a picture of Khamenei's clenched fist on a red and black background. Red stands for grief and a call for revenge. Black stands for martyrdom (dying for a cause). A giant red flag has been hung over the Grand Mosalla, Tehran's biggest religious building. It says "O avengers of Hussein" in Arabic. This refers to a story from 1,300 years ago when the Prophet Muhammad's grandson was killed. The message is that revenge against the US and Israel is a religious duty. Khamenei's body is being taken on a tour through important cities in Iran and Iraq, like Qom, Najaf, and Karbala. These places are very holy in Shia Islam, the main religion in Iran. The tour ends in Mashhad, where Khamenei will be buried. His son Mojtaba Khamenei is now the new Supreme Leader, but he hasn't been seen in public because of security risks. So the funeral is also a way to show unity and strength.
why_it_matters: Even a funeral can be about more than sadness — it shows how powerful symbols and traditions can unite a whole country and express strong feelings.

background_read: Iran is a large country in the Middle East, and its government includes both elected officials and religious leaders. The Supreme Leader has the highest authority.
The funeral is for Ayatollah Ali Khamenei (the former Supreme Leader of Iran), who died in a US-Israeli airstrike earlier in the year. The scale of the ceremonies helped show his importance.
Shia Islam, the branch of Islam practiced by most Iranians, has a long history of honoring martyrs. Cities like Qom, Najaf, and Karbala are considered very holy places.
Article_Structure: WHO: Ayatollah Ali Khamenei (the former Supreme Leader) and his son Mojtaba, who is now the new Supreme Leader.
WHAT: A huge funeral that is also a political rally, using colors, slogans, and flags to call for revenge against the US and Israel.
WHERE: In Iran, with a giant red flag at the Grand Mosalla in Tehran, and a tour through important holy cities like Qom, Najaf, Karbala, and burial in Mashhad.
WHY: The ceremonies aim to unite the country, show strength, and send a message that revenge is a religious responsibility.

perspectives.description: They see the funeral as a way to honor a great leader and show the world that Iran will stand up to its enemies.
Some worry that calling for revenge so strongly could lead to more fighting and make it harder to find peace.
They notice how old religious stories and symbols are used to make political points, mixing faith and national power.
